paper_title: Robustly federated learning model for identifying high-risk patients with postoperative gastric cancer recurrence
prediction_task: Postoperative gastric cancer recurrence prediction via federated learning across 4 centers

reviewer_concerns.concern_text: How did they define and evaluate recurrence after surgery? Specific recurrence types (peritoneal) and their distribution needed. Follow-up duration and frequency not provided.
reviewer_concerns.author_response: Added recurrence type distribution, follow-up protocol details.

reviewer_concerns.concern_text: Class imbalance between centers may affect federated learning convergence. This is very important for clinical application but not evaluated or discussed.
reviewer_concerns.author_response: Added class balance analysis per center and convergence diagnostics.

reviewer_concerns.concern_text: Too many different adjectives for features ('common', 'distinct', 'individual', 'personality information', etc.) — need to be consolidated and precisely defined. Discussion in Results section difficult before model details are provided.
More details needed to evaluate privacy properties. Should include pseudo-code showing exactly what information is transmitted between sites.
reviewer_concerns.author_response: Added privacy protocol pseudo-code and communication analysis.

reviewer_concerns.concern_text: Need table with sufficient clinical information for all patients — tumor stage, gender, age distributions. How many radiologists defined ROI? For gastric cancer, tumor area identification is difficult.
reviewer_concerns.author_response: Added demographics table and ROI annotation protocol.

reviewer_strengths.text: Impressive results on cross-silo federated learning problem. Promising approach for multi-center data handling and privacy preservation.
